experience.title: Web & Product Consultant
experience.description: After leaving The Motley Fool I took some time to travel, hike the Appalachian Trail, and think about what I wanted to build next. In 2024 I completed the Climatebase Fellowship, a structured cohort program that gave me a foundation in the climate space. Since then I've been consulting for small businesses on product, SEO, and web, and spending a lot of time building with AI tools — the most energizing stretch of learning I've had in a while.
highlights: Completed the Climatebase Fellowship (2024), a structured program for professionals transitioning into climate-focused roles
Provide ongoing product, SEO, and web consulting for small businesses, including Wild Blue Travel

Built several AI-assisted personal projects using Claude Code, including What Mile?, an interactive map-based geography guessing game, and Carbon Tracker, a browser widget for tracking website carbon footprint

experience.title: Career Break — Appalachian Trail Thru-hike
experience.description: Completed 2,190-mile thru-hike of the Appalachian Trail, demonstrating exceptional perseverance, planning, and long-term goal achievement in challenging, resource-constrained conditions.

experience.title: Product Lead
experience.description: The Motley Fool is where product management became my full-time focus. I joined as a Technical SEO Strategist, sat with the product team, and worked directly with developers on technical implementation. Within a few months I was promoted to Product Owner for fool.com, a big role at a company that ran almost entirely on content and organic reach. I spent the next two-plus years there, eventually moving into a Product Lead role to head up a new subscription initiative.
highlights: Led development of new customer acquisition product from discovery to pre-launch, conducting user research, creating interactive demos that secured executive approval, and achieving positive early user feedback
Launched a unified member dashboard serving millions of users, consolidating multiple product experiences into a single interface that improved engagement and navigation
Partnered with engineering teams to define technical requirements and product specifications for a new subscription product, writing detailed epics and user stories to guide development
Collaborated with CEO, executive team, designers, and engineers to introduce new product development methodology, facilitating workshops that improved cross-functional alignment

experience.title: Product Owner
experience.description: Owned product roadmap and strategy for fool.com with millions of monthly visitors.
highlights: Owned product roadmap and strategy for fool.com (millions of monthly visitors), driving 20%+ improvement in engagement metrics through data-driven prioritization
Used SQL and analytics platforms to independently query data, analyze user behavior patterns, and inform feature development and roadmap decisions
Facilitated cross-functional discovery sessions with engineering, design, and marketing to identify user pain points and align on product priorities
Shipped multiple features balancing user needs, technical complexity, and business objectives

experience.title: Technical SEO Strategist
experience.description: Developed technical SEO strategy and bridged communication between technical and non-technical teams.
highlights: Developed technical strategy presentation for President and CTO, translating complex technical concepts for executive audience and facilitating company-wide workshops
Bridged communication between technical and non-technical teams to drive adoption of best practices across the organization

experience.title: SEO Lead
experience.description: Cvent brought me back east after Zillow. The role was narrower than expected — focused on the marketing site with limited reach into the broader product and engineering organization — and it became clear quickly that the path I was looking for wasn't there.
highlights: Led global SEO strategy, advising executives on technical recommendations and building implementation roadmaps across engineering, product, and marketing teams

experience.title: Product Manager, SEO
experience.description: HotPads was one of four Zillow Group rental properties — and unlike its siblings, it ran almost entirely on organic search. No marketing team, no paid acquisition. Just Google, email notifications, and push alerts for repeat visits. That made SEO existential, not just strategic.
highlights: Built and launched the SEO Links API in close collaboration with engineering, reducing front-end server calls by ~10% and improving crawl efficiency across the site

When a Google Quality algorithm update caused a 20%+ overnight traffic drop, led the diagnosis: deep research, industry networking, and direct consultation with Google alumni inside Zillow to understand the update's intent
Concluded the real fix was long-term investment in content quality and user experience — not technical quick wins — and designed a roadmap accordingly

Shipped the Nearby Listings widget to reduce bounce rates on long-tail pages with no inventory, and added in-page filter prompts after data showed that users who changed filters spent more time, visited more pages, and submitted more inquiries

experience.title: Sr SEO Account Manager
experience.description: Merkle is where I started, and where I figured out what kind of work I actually wanted to do. I came in as a paid search analyst, switched to SEO once I realized how deeply it was entangled with web development, and got promoted nearly every year: specialist, senior specialist, account manager, senior account manager. I managed an eclectic client portfolio across various industries, including aviation wire, flowers, nationwide retailers, and a UK tabloid, because I enjoyed the challenge that came with learning and understanding different businesses. By the end I'd hit a ceiling, and knew I was more interested in building than managing campaigns.
highlights: Pitched and led a full site architecture and content buildout for A.E. Petsche (Arrow Electronics), growing their site from roughly 20 pages to hundreds of targeted product and category pages, creating the organic search presence they had essentially none of before

Restructured how the team operated: shifted specialists from support roles into owning their accounts directly, which improved work quality and freed managers to focus on strategy rather than being a communication layer

Coached a team of five with different approaches for each person, from giving high-initiative team members autonomy to run with projects, to intensive preparation work that helped a less confident team member lead client calls independently
